excluded_seen: The first look (examples/scale-up-compete, exploratory), under the draw only: the two pairs on 128 x 128 from starts 9001 to 9016, and soups from rule sets 9001 to 9012 and starts 9001 to 9008. The margins and thresholds here were set from its means and spreads. No registered start or rule set is among them.
Two earlier counts of contested births, under the draw only: Life against itself and against HighLife on 256 x 256, and 24 autorun sessions with autorun's own random rules.

Under the standoff: one run of Life against HighLife on 128 x 128 from start 1 for 500 generations (the example in LatticeLife's docs), of which only that neither species died out was read; and three autorun sessions with autorun's own random rules, of which only the schema and the total of contested cells were read. LatticeLife's tests and this study's run both tie-breaks on grids of side 16 to 32 from other starts.
No registered world has been run under either tie-break. The registered soups' rules (sets 1 to 24) were generated to write this entry, and nothing was run on them.
body.intervals: Welch's interval for the difference of two means (standoff minus draw), Student's for one mean; 99%, and 99.9% for the known answer S
body.source: docs/scale-up-plan.md, decision D1; the first look in examples/scale-up-compete
body.statement: Life-like pairs and five-species soups on wrapped square grids, half full at the start with the species in equal shares, are run under the random draw and under the standoff from the same starts. Identical species end level under both (S). Where contests are rare the two tie-breaks give the same live fraction, species balance and mixing (A, and B0 for soups). Where contests are common the standoff changes the live fraction, and lowers it (B1, B2).
